scope: Rio Grande Valley (Hidalgo, Cameron, Starr, Willacy) - healthcare, mental health, school/childcare, employment, legal

records.name: Mental Health & Substance Use Crisis Hotline
records.description_en: A 24-hour phone line for anyone having a mental health or substance use crisis in the Rio Grande Valley. Trained staff can talk with you and connect you to help.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Anyone in the Rio Grande Valley who is in crisis, or worried about someone who is.
records.how_to_apply: Call the crisis hotline any time, day or night. For TTY, call 1-800-735-2988. If there is immediate danger, call 911.
records.hours: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week
records.cost: Free
records.notes: TTBH is the public mental health center for the Rio Grande Valley. The website does not list its counties by name. The national 988 line is another option.

records.name: TTBH Edinburg Outpatient Clinic
records.description_en: An outpatient clinic for children and adults. Mental health, intellectual and developmental disability (IDD), and substance use services, plus a peer drop-in center.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Rio Grande Valley residents who need mental health, IDD, or substance use care. Adult services are for ages 18 and up. Child and youth services are for ages 3 to 17.
records.how_to_apply: Call 1-800-813-1233 to make an appointment or ask questions. In a crisis, call 1-877-289-7199.
records.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; Thursday until 7:00 PM (adult mental health); first Saturday of each month 8:00 AM-12:00 PM (children's services)
records.cost: Accepts Medicaid, Medicare and many insurance plans; sliding fee scale; no one is denied services for inability to pay.
records.notes: The ZIP code is not listed on the source page. TTBH also has a McAllen clinic; call 1-800-813-1233 for its address.

records.name: TTBH Weslaco Outpatient Clinic
records.description_en: An outpatient clinic for children and adults. Mental health, IDD, and substance use services, plus a veterans center.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Rio Grande Valley residents who need mental health, IDD, or substance use care. Adult services are for ages 18 and up. Child and youth services are for ages 3 to 17.
records.how_to_apply: Call 1-800-813-1233 to make an appointment or ask questions. In a crisis, call 1-877-289-7199.
records.cost: Accepts Medicaid, Medicare and many insurance plans; sliding fee scale; no one is denied services for inability to pay.
records.notes: The ZIP code is not listed on the source page. TTBH also has a McAllen clinic; call 1-800-813-1233 for its address.

records.name: TTBH Harlingen Outpatient Clinic
records.description_en: An outpatient clinic for children and adults. Adult mental health, IDD, and substance use services.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Rio Grande Valley residents who need mental health, IDD, or substance use care. Adult services are for ages 18 and up. Child and youth services are for ages 3 to 17.
records.how_to_apply: Call 1-800-813-1233 to make an appointment or ask questions. In a crisis, call 1-877-289-7199.
records.cost: Accepts Medicaid, Medicare and many insurance plans; sliding fee scale; no one is denied services for inability to pay.
records.notes: The ZIP code is not listed on the source page. TTBH also has a McAllen clinic; call 1-800-813-1233 for its address.

records.name: TTBH Brownsville Outpatient Clinic
records.description_en: An outpatient clinic for children and adults. General mental health services and a veterans center.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Rio Grande Valley residents who need mental health, IDD, or substance use care. Adult services are for ages 18 and up. Child and youth services are for ages 3 to 17.
records.how_to_apply: Call 1-800-813-1233 to make an appointment or ask questions. In a crisis, call 1-877-289-7199.
records.cost: Accepts Medicaid, Medicare and many insurance plans; sliding fee scale; no one is denied services for inability to pay.
records.notes: The ZIP code is not listed on the source page. TTBH also has a McAllen clinic; call 1-800-813-1233 for its address.

records.name: Veteran Services
records.description_en: Counseling for veterans with depression, anxiety, or PTSD, plus substance use treatment, peer support, family support, and help getting VA benefits.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Veterans and their families in the Rio Grande Valley.
records.how_to_apply: Call 1-800-813-1233 for an appointment or visit a veterans center. Centers are in Weslaco (2215 W. Business 83, 956-520-8860), Harlingen (1242 N. 77 Sunshine Strip, 956-423-1233), and Brownsville (871 Old Alice Rd. Suite C, 956-547-1510).
records.cost: Accepts Medicaid, Medicare and many insurance plans; sliding fee scale; no one is denied services for inability to pay.
records.notes: The Veterans Crisis Line is also available: dial 988, then press 1.

records.name: Intellectual & Developmental Disability (IDD) Services
records.description_en: Help for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities. It includes service coordination, day programs, respite care for caregivers, and help getting and keeping a job.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Children and adults with intellectual or developmental disabilities in the Rio Grande Valley. Staff check if you qualify at intake.
records.how_to_apply: Call the IDD line at (956) 289-7233 to ask about an intake and assessment.
records.cost: Accepts Medicaid, Medicare and many insurance plans; sliding fee scale; no one is denied services for inability to pay.
records.notes: The page mentions Early Childhood Intervention for children up to age 3 and YES Waiver services for youth.

records.name: Outreach, Screening, Assessment and Referral (OSAR)
records.description_en: Helps people who need treatment for drug or alcohol use. Staff screen you and connect you to the right level of care.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Anyone in the Rio Grande Valley who needs help with substance use.
records.how_to_apply: Call 1-800-813-1233 to get screened. In a crisis, call 1-877-289-7199.
records.cost: Contact TTBH about cost. TTBH uses a sliding fee scale and does not turn people away for inability to pay.
records.notes: This program serves Health Region 11.

records.name: Substance Use Prevention, Treatment & Recovery Services
records.organization: Behavioral Health Solutions of South Texas
records.description_en: Outpatient treatment, counseling, recovery support groups, and free naloxone for people dealing with drug or alcohol use. It also runs parenting and youth programs.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Youth and adults in Cameron, Hidalgo, and Willacy Counties. Some programs also serve Starr County. Treatment is open to people with or without insurance.
records.how_to_apply: Call (956) 787-7111 and ask for the program you need. For example, ask for treatment at extension 221.
records.cost: Most prevention and recovery programs are free. Some treatment programs, such as Fueling Hope, are free.
records.notes: Services are offered in person, at home, by video, or by phone. Treatment programs include Fueling Hope and Empowering Hope (adults 18+) and Monarch (ages 13-17).

records.name: Hope Family Health Center
records.description_en: A nonprofit safety-net clinic for uninsured, low-income families. It offers primary care, women's health, labs, medicines for patients who qualify, and counseling. Case coordinators can help with rent, food, transportation, and child care resources.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Uninsured, low-income people in the Rio Grande Valley. The clinic currently sees patients age 6 and older.
records.how_to_apply: Call (956) 994-3319 or email office@hfhcenter.org to ask about becoming a patient.
records.hours: Monday-Thursday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; Friday 8:00 AM-1:30 PM (closed holidays)
records.cost: The source does not list fees. Services are funded by donors and grants.
records.notes: One page lists pediatric care from age 2, but the medical and counseling pages say ages 6 and up. The site says it serves the Rio Grande Valley but does not name counties; Hidalgo County is listed because the clinic is in McAllen.

records.name: Domestic Violence & Sexual Assault Services
records.description_en: Help for survivors of domestic violence and sexual assault. It includes a 24/7 hotline, emergency shelter, transitional housing, counseling, a rape crisis center, and legal advocacy.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Survivors of domestic violence or sexual assault in the Rio Grande Valley, especially women and children.
records.how_to_apply: Call the 24/7 hotline at 1-877-580-4879. The main office number is (956) 630-4878.
records.hours: Hotline 24/7. Office: Monday-Thursday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM, Friday 8:00 AM-4:00 PM, closed 12:00-1:00 PM
records.notes: There is also a satellite center at 420 N. 21st Street, McAllen (956-664-2826). The site does not list costs or name the counties it serves.

records.name: Nuestra Clinica del Valle - San Juan Clinic
records.description_en: A community health center that provides medical care for the whole family. Nuestra Clinica also offers dental, behavioral health, pharmacy, and lab services across its clinics.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Everyone is welcome, whether or not they can pay. People without insurance can pay on a sliding fee scale based on income.
documents_needed: Photo ID
Insurance card (Medicaid, CHIP, Medicare, county or private), if you have one
Proof of income (if uninsured, for the sliding fee scale)
records.how_to_apply: Call or visit the clinic to become a patient. You can fill out the patient registration form from the website ahead of time.
records.hours: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; night clinic Tuesdays 6:00-9:00 PM
records.cost: Sliding fee scale for uninsured patients; accepts Medicaid, Medicare, CHIP and most private insurance
records.notes: The main line is (956) 787-0787. Services differ by clinic, so check which services this location offers. Outreach staff can help with CHIP and Medicaid applications.

records.name: Su Clinica Brownsville
records.description_en: A federally qualified community health center. It offers pediatrics, women's health, adult medicine, behavioral health, and dental care, plus an on-site pharmacy, lab, and x-ray.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to the community. As a federally qualified health center, it can lower fees based on family size and income.
documents_needed: The items on Su Clinica's Registration Checklist (ask the clinic)
records.how_to_apply: Visit the clinic and meet with a Registration Specialist. They will check which programs you qualify for. Call (956) 365-6000 to ask whether the clinic is taking new patients.
records.hours: Pediatrics Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-8:30 PM and Saturday-Sunday 11:00 AM-4:30 PM; Adult Medicine Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; Women's Health Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM
records.cost: Sliding fee based on family size and income; accepts Medicaid, Medicare and most private insurance
records.notes: Some locations may not be accepting new patients. A free after-hours nurse line is available at (956) 365-6000.

records.name: Cameron County Indigent Health Care Program
records.description_en: Basic health care for very low-income county residents who do not qualify for Medicaid or other programs. It covers doctor visits, screenings, yearly checkups, shots, labs and x-rays, hospital care, and up to 3 prescriptions a month.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Cameron County residents who do not qualify for Medicaid, with household income at or below 21% of the federal poverty guidelines. Household resources must be $2,000 or less, or $3,000 or less if someone in the home is 60+ or disabled.
records.how_to_apply: Pick up an application at the Brownsville or San Benito office and make an appointment.
records.cost: Free
records.notes: San Benito office: 1390 W. Expressway 83, San Benito, TX 78586, (956) 247-3665. Care is limited to participating providers.

records.name: Cameron County Public Health Clinics
records.description_en: Low-cost or free preventive care, including family planning, shots for children and adults, prenatal and child health, STD testing and treatment, and TB care.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Eligible Cameron County residents, with a focus on uninsured and low-income families.
records.how_to_apply: Call (956) 247-3685 to check if you qualify or to ask for services. You can also call one of the clinics.
records.cost: Minimal to no cost
records.notes: Clinics: Mary P. Lucio Health Center, 1204 Jose Colunga Jr. St., Brownsville (956-574-8745); San Benito Public Health Clinic (956-361-8244); Harlingen Public Health Center, 711 N. L St. (956-423-3516); Father Joseph O'Brien Health Clinic, 142 Champion Ave, Port Isabel.

records.name: Cameron County WIC Program
records.description_en: Healthy foods, nutrition classes, and breastfeeding support for pregnant women, new mothers, babies, and children under 5.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Pregnant or breastfeeding women, women who had a baby in the last 6 months, and children under 5. Families on Medicaid, TANF, or SNAP meet the income rule. You do not have to be a U.S. citizen.
records.how_to_apply: Start an application online at texaswic.org or call 1-888-942-4847.
records.cost: Free
records.notes: There are 12 clinics, including Brownsville (several), Harlingen (711 N. L St., 956-423-3516), San Benito, Los Fresnos, Port Isabel, Rio Hondo, and Santa Rosa. FAQ and eligibility details: https://www.cameroncountytx.gov/publichealth/wic-program/

records.name: Hidalgo County WIC Program
records.description_en: Healthy foods, nutrition counseling, breastfeeding support, and referrals for pregnant and postpartum women, infants, and children up to age 5. A mobile unit visits communities.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Pregnant, breastfeeding, and postpartum women, infants, and children under 5 in households at or below 185% of the federal poverty line. People on Medicaid, TANF, or SNAP meet the income rule. U.S. citizenship is not required.
records.how_to_apply: Call (956) 381-4646 to make an appointment. Your nutrition risk is checked at the first visit.
records.cost: Free
records.notes: The program serves Hidalgo and Starr Counties. Clinics include Alamo II, Hidalgo, Progreso, San Carlos, Sullivan City, and a mobile unit. For special accommodations, call (956) 279-7850. Income chart: https://www.hidalgocounty.us/1010/WIC-Eligibility-Requirements

records.name: Hidalgo County Indigent Health Care Program
records.description_en: A county program that pays for basic health care, such as doctor visits, labs, and x-rays, for very low-income residents who cannot get Medicaid.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Hidalgo County residents who do not qualify for Medicaid and who meet strict income and resource limits. Texas sets the limit at or below 21% of federal poverty guidelines, with resources under $2,000.
records.how_to_apply: Call Hidalgo County Health & Human Services at (956) 383-6221 and ask about the County Indigent Health Care Program.
records.cost: Free
records.notes: The county website has no current program page. Only a 2016 flyer (hidalgocounty.us/documentcenter/view/22872) confirms that Health & Human Services runs the program. Income and resource limits come from the HHSC CIHCP page (hhs.texas.gov/services/health/county-indigent-health-care-program). Call to confirm details.

records.name: Hidalgo County Head Start & Early Head Start
records.description_en: Free early education for young children, plus health, dental, nutrition, mental health, and family support services. Head Start is for ages 3-4. Early Head Start is for birth to age 2.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Families in Hidalgo County with young children. Families on TANF, SNAP, or SSI, children in foster care, and homeless families are automatically eligible, if space allows.
documents_needed: Child's birth certificate or baptismal record
Proof of all sources of income
Utility statement
records.how_to_apply: Fill out the online pre-application on the Head Start website, or call (956) 383-0706.
records.cost: Free
records.notes: Early Head Start campuses are in Donna, Mission, and San Juan. Head Start campuses are across Hidalgo County. Office address and phone come from https://www.hidalgocounty.us/1110/Head-Start-Program. max_age 4 is the child's age.

records.name: Child Care Services (child care scholarships)
records.organization: Workforce Solutions (Lower Rio Grande Valley Workforce Development Board)
records.description_en: Helps income-eligible parents pay for child care while they work, go to school or training, or look for a job. Parents choose their own licensed provider.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Parents in Hidalgo, Starr, or Willacy County earning 85% of State Median Income or less. They must need care to work or go to school at least 25 hours a week (50 hours combined for two parents), or to look for work. Parents on TANF or SNAP job programs may also qualify.
documents_needed: Proof of income (pay stubs; if paid in cash, an Employment/Income Verification Form)
Previous year's income tax form
records.how_to_apply: Create an account on TX3C Parent Central and complete the Eligibility Screener & Waitlist Application. For help, call the Mission (956-519-4300) or Weslaco (956-969-6100) office.
records.cost: Parent co-pay on a sliding scale based on income and family size. Initial job search care is available for up to 3 months.
records.notes: If you lose your job, report it within 14 days. Parents in school full time without work have a 60-month limit. Fee reductions are possible for unexpected expenses. The apply_url is the TX3C sign-up link from Workforce Solutions Cameron's site.

records.name: Child Care Services
records.description_en: Helps income-eligible families in Cameron County find and pay for child care. New families may get up to 3 months of care with no co-pay while looking for work.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Income-eligible Cameron County families who need child care to work, go to school, or look for work. There is a waitlist.
documents_needed: Employment Verification Form or Self Employment Verification Form (as needed)
records.how_to_apply: Submit the pre-screener and waitlist application online through Texas Child Care Connection (TX3C). You will be asked every 90 days if you still need care, and you must answer within 10 business days to stay on the list.
records.cost: Co-pay based on income once work requirements are met
records.notes: To keep care after 3 months of initial job search, parents must work 25 hours a week (single parent) or 50 hours combined (two parents). Harlingen office: (956) 423-9266.

records.name: Workforce Solutions Edinburg Office
records.organization: Workforce Solutions (Lower Rio Grande Valley Workforce Development Board)
records.description_en: A free job center. Staff help with job searches, resumes, career counseling, and workshops. They can also help you apply for training money and child care assistance.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Anyone looking for work. To get personalized job or training services, you must show papers proving you are allowed to work in the U.S.
documents_needed: Work authorization documents (one item from List A, or one from List B and one from List C)
records.how_to_apply: Visit the office or call (888) 261-3286 to schedule an appointment. You can also search jobs on WorkInTexas.com.
records.cost: Free
records.notes: Serves Hidalgo, Starr, and Willacy Counties. In-person and virtual services are available. For training (WIOA) appointments, call (956) 687-1121.

records.notes: Serves Hidalgo, Starr, and Willacy Counties. In-person and virtual services are available. For training (WIOA) appointments, call (956) 687-1121.

records.name: Workforce Solutions Willacy County Office
records.organization: Workforce Solutions (Lower Rio Grande Valley Workforce Development Board)
records.description_en: A free job center. Staff help with job searches, resumes, career counseling, and workshops. They can also help you apply for training money and child care assistance.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Anyone looking for work. To get personalized job or training services, you must show papers proving you are allowed to work in the U.S.
documents_needed: Work authorization documents (one item from List A, or one from List B and one from List C)
records.how_to_apply: Visit the office or call (888) 261-3286 to schedule an appointment. You can also search jobs on WorkInTexas.com.
records.cost: Free
records.notes: Serves Hidalgo, Starr, and Willacy Counties. In-person and virtual services are available. For training (WIOA) appointments, call (956) 687-1121.

records.name: E3 Youth Program (Empower - Educate - Employ)
records.organization: Workforce Solutions (Lower Rio Grande Valley Workforce Development Board)
records.description_en: Helps young people get paid work experience, job-readiness training, mentoring, career counseling, and help with training or school costs.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Young people ages 16-24 in Hidalgo, Starr, or Willacy County who need money, want a paid internship, or want to build job skills. Other eligibility rules apply.
records.how_to_apply: Schedule an appointment online or call (888) 261-3286.
records.cost: Free
records.notes: ASL interpreters are available if you ask 3 business days ahead.

records.name: Workforce Solutions Cameron - Brownsville Center
records.description_en: A free job center for Cameron County. It offers job listings, hiring events, help with resumes and job searches, training money, and help with child care services.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Job seekers and employers in Cameron County.
records.how_to_apply: Visit the center during business hours or call. You can also search for jobs on WorkInTexas.com.
records.cost: Free
records.notes: Corporate office: 700 Ruben M. Torres Blvd., 3rd Floor, Brownsville. Relay Texas: 711.

records.name: WIOA Occupational Training Assistance
records.description_en: Pays for job training in high-demand jobs. It can also cover books, tools, transportation, work clothes, on-the-job training, and referrals for child care.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Cameron County low-income adults 18 and older, workers who were laid off, and low-income youth ages 14-24 with a barrier (for example, dropped out of school, pregnant or parenting, homeless, or disabled).
records.how_to_apply: Visit a Workforce Solutions Cameron center or call (956) 546-3141 to see if you qualify. Training must come from a provider on the state Eligible Training Provider list.
records.cost: Free to eligible participants
records.notes: Laid-off workers may qualify as dislocated workers.

records.name: Adult Continuing Education (A.C.E.) - GED & English Classes
records.organization: Adult Continuing Education (A.C.E.), partner of Workforce Solutions Cameron
records.description_en: Free GED classes, English classes, job certifications (like Microsoft Office Specialist), and classes to help adults move on to college or a job. Online distance learning is available.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Adults who live in Cameron County.
records.how_to_apply: Fill out the enrollment form on the Workforce Solutions Cameron website, then call (956) 548-8175 to schedule a visit.
records.cost: Free
records.notes: English classes are held in Harlingen, La Feria, Los Fresnos, Port Isabel, San Benito, and Brownsville. There is a Welcome Back Center for immigrants with college degrees.

records.name: VIDA Workforce Training Program
records.organization: Valley Initiative for Development and Advancement (VIDA)
records.description_en: Helps low-income adults train for well-paying careers. It offers help with tuition and school costs, counseling, and weekly support sessions. Programs include nursing, patient care tech, diesel and automotive tech, electrician, EMT/paramedic, and police academy.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Low-income Rio Grande Valley residents who want training for a high-demand career. The website does not list exact eligibility rules.
records.how_to_apply: Start an application through the intake portal on VIDA's website, or call (956) 903-1900.
records.cost: The website does not list costs. VIDA provides financial help for training.
records.notes: Toll-free: (800) 478-1770. The site mentions McAllen, Pharr, Mercedes, Harlingen, and Brownsville but does not list counties, so Starr and Willacy are not included. Confirm eligibility with VIDA.

records.name: Free Civil Legal Aid - Edinburg Office
records.description_en: Free civil legal help for low-income people. This includes family law, housing and eviction, subsidized housing, foreclosure, employment, farmworker, and civil rights cases.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Low-income residents of TRLA's 68-county service area in Southwest Texas, which includes the Rio Grande Valley. TRLA screens callers for income and case type.
records.how_to_apply: Call (956) 996-8752 (toll-free 833-329-8752) on weekdays from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM to apply for free legal help.
records.hours: Phone intake: Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM Central
records.cost: Free
records.notes: TRLA will never ask for payment or bank details. The Mercedes headquarters (301 S. Texas) has administrative staff only and does no intake. The county listed for each office is a best guess based on location; the central intake line serves all four counties.
